pr_title: network: process queued remove requests on stop
pr_body:
Fixes a regression caused by 85a6f300c14d75d161cbfdb3eaf5af9594400ecd and its later commits. 
Fixes #34837.
pr_comments: I rebased this on 256 (one very simple conflict) and it appears to have resolved the issue.

issue_context.title: systemd-networkd fails to drop routes & addresses on stop with `KeepConfiguration=no`
issue_context.body:
### systemd version the issue has been seen with

~~v255.6~~ v256 onwards, reproduces on v256.4

### Used distribution

NixOS unstable 24.11pre-git (since `a5b2fe73` up to `5633bcf`)

### Linux kernel version used

Both 6.6.54-xanmod1, 6.6.54

### CPU architectures issue was seen on

x86_64

### Component

systemd-networkd

### Expected behaviour you didn't see

`[Network].KeepConfiguration=no` is respected and networkd drops IPv4 addresses when stopped

### Unexpected behaviour you saw

After `SYSTEMD_LOG_LEVEL=debug systemctl import-environment SYSTEMD_LOG_LEVEL && systemctl restart systemd-networkd`, networkd logs show that it is attempting to drop addresses and routes but `ip r` and `ip a` show they are still present. With `networkctl down eth0`, this does not happen.

### Steps to reproduce the problem

Run the `systemd-initrd-networkd.doFlush` NixOS test from a nixpkgs newer than 2024-07-29.

Observe [it fails](https://hydra.nixos.org/build/267693996): ([full logs](https://cache.nixos.org/log/69432jppr8pfpjp3aq0z5bs8ri9d5f84-vm-test-run-systemd-initrd-network-flush.drv))
```
[   12.832587] check-flush-start[352]:     inet 10.0.2.15/24 metric 1024 brd 10.0.2.255 scope global dynamic eth0
[   12.837278] check-flush-start[345]: Network configuration survived switch-root; flushBeforeStage2 failed
```

```
$ networkctl cat 99-ethernet-default-dhcp.network
# /etc/systemd/network/99-ethernet-default-dhcp.network
[Match]
Name=en*
Name=eth*
 
[Network]
DHCP=yes
IPv6PrivacyExtensions=kernel
KeepConfiguration=no # KeepConfiguration is set
```

### Additional program output to the terminal or log subsystem illustrating the issue

`networkctl down eth0` correctly drops address:
https://gist.github.com/ckiee/53c0bcdcedbee8f985563cf3fbb8bea0

`systemctl stop systemd-networkd` tries to drop addresses and routes but fails.
https://gist.github.com/ckiee/b30551342e3d05722916c1e34bf007fc
comments: Correction, I believe v255.6 is unaffected by this. The first known affected version seems to be v256.

It looks like `address_remove_handler` is never getting called after `address_remove` while `systemd-networkd` shuts down, which is because `manager_post_handler` is never called to handle the request that was queued by `link_remove_request_add`. I think the DHCP lease is being released, but the address is not being removed from the link.
Indeed... Thank you for the report. I will take a look.
@ElvishJerricco Thank you for the proposal. I submitted a patch in #34871 that fixes the issue in a similar but slightly different way. PTAL.
